_comment: Ratchet config for scripts/codecharta-ratchet.py, run against the CodeCharta map (ortus.cc.json.gz). Three gates: (1) per-file aggregate complexity, (2) per-FUNCTION complexity (not gameable by moving code between files), (3) hotspot (complex AND under-tested), plus go coverage. Ratchet by LOWERING the numbers as the code improves; RAISING a baseline entry needs review justification.

complexity._default_cap_note: Per-file SUM of function complexity. Every file not listed below must stay <= this. This gate stops a file becoming a monolith, but can be satisfied by splitting a file (the sum moves with the code) — see function_complexity for the non-gameable ceiling. Current highest non-baseline file is 40 (internal/adapters/storage/http.go).
complexity._raster_repository_note: raster/repository.go raised 143→149 for the persistent extraction-cache feature (Open now branches ephemeral/persistent). The bulk of the new logic is in cache.go; the per-function cap stayed 15 (no function grew) — genuine new branching, not relocation.
complexity._batch_note: geopackage/repository.go 127→128 (buildFeature extracted from scanFeature to enable batch reuse), application/registry.go 79→86 (QueryPoints batch seam + a context-cancellation guard in the non-batch fallback loop so a disconnected client aborts early — review-requested correctness fix), config/config.go 72→79 (query.batch.* config + validation), http/handlers.go 70→72 (handleQueryError now maps propagated context.DeadlineExceeded→504 and context.Canceled→499 for the batch path — two error-classification cases) — all for the batch-query endpoint. Per-function caps unchanged; the bulk of batch logic lives in new batch.go files.
complexity._bearing_inside_note: application/gazetteer/bearing.go 55→68: the 'in {X}' decision moved from admin-containment to a class-scaled distance gate (placeInsideOf + nearestInClassWithin, per-class within each class's own radius so a qualifying town/city isn't hidden behind nearer out-of-radius villages). Fixes points far inside a large municipality being labelled 'in <village>'. Review round added the country+tier guard (admits) to the 'in' path so a place across a state line isn't reported as inside, consistent with anchor selection (→72). Per-function cap unchanged.
complexity._islands_dedup_note: application/gazetteer/service.go 68→69: Islands now dedups by name (a same-name island duplicated in the data — two OSM objects for one island — must appear once), one added branch.
complexity._builtup_gate_note: application/gazetteer/bearing.go 72→73 and application/gazetteer/service.go 69→74: optional built-up gate for the 'in <place>' decision. bearing.go gains one branch — the 'in' path only runs when builtUpAllows(p) holds. service.go gains SetBuiltUpSampler wiring plus builtUpAllows, which short-circuits to distance-only when no sampler is wired or the point has no built-up coverage, otherwise requires the sampled built-up value to meet the configured minimum (suppresses 'in <village>' on fields/parks within a place's radius), and fails CLOSED on a sampler error (review-requested: an unhealthy raster must not silently re-open an unverified 'in'). Sampler + adapter live in new files (ports/output/builtup.go, adapters/raster/builtup.go, app/builtup.go); per-function caps unchanged. internal/app/app.go ratcheted 83→82 (map re-measure).
complexity._mountains_note: New gazetteer 'mountains' block (smallest containing range + single-mountain per landform, mirroring islands): application/gazetteer/service.go 0→68 baselined (Mountains + smallestByLandform + mountainFrom + moreSpecific), http/gazetteer.go 0→57 baselined (addMountains + formatMountains + formatMountain). Per-function: gazetteerSections 13→14 and the MCP gazetteer handler 13→14 (one new optional block each, same inline pattern as islands/elevation); the mountains block was extracted to addMountains to keep gazetteerSections at +1 rather than +2.

baseline._timings_note: gazetteerSections gained per-section wall-clock timing (a mark() closure + 6 mark() calls) to surface the DEM-derived exposure/elevation enrichment cost that processing_time_ms omits; +1 file complexity (57→58) and +1 function complexity (14→15, = current repo max) for that observability. Sub-functions were not extractable without splitting the section sequence.
baseline._note_spatialindex: 54 -> 67 (2026-08-23): TableColumns + SpatialLayers, reporting each declared table's columns and which tables are registered feature layers, so the manifest can be checked against the file at startup. Previously a manifest naming a table or column that is not there produced empty results indistinguishable from a legitimate 'nothing found'. Both facts are needed: columns alone do not make a queryable layer, since every read resolves its geometry column through gpkg_geometry_columns first, so a plain SQLite table with the right names would pass a columns-only check and then fail every query. The judgement itself lives in Manifest.VerifyAgainst, deliberately not here — the adapter only reports facts, which is what kept the file from growing further.
baseline._note_handlers: 72 -> 75 (2026-08-23): the gazetteer identity block on /sources (dataset_version/built), field-wise omitted when unset so an absent value is never reported as blank. Three guard clauses for a deployed package that could otherwise not be told apart from any other build of the same file name.
baseline._note_service: 74 -> 77 (2026-08-23): Capabilities(), reporting which optional blocks the loaded dataset can answer, plus the branch that distinguishes a point outside the DEM (no elevation block) from water inside it (sea level). Both exist because a null block used to mean two different things — absent from the dataset, or no result here — and the second is a normal answer since the territory run-out cap.
baseline._note_raster_repository: 149 -> 162 (2026-08-23): CoverageAt, reporting whether a layer covers a point regardless of whether that pixel holds a value. QueryPoint returns 'no feature' for two unrelated reasons — beyond the raster's footprint, or inside it on a nodata pixel — and for a DEM that difference is water versus unknown. Elevation used to report both as sea level, i.e. it asserted 0 m for ground outside the DEM, which is a confident wrong answer exactly at the coverage edge. The shared layerOf lookup was extracted so the query and coverage paths cannot disagree about where coverage ends; that was worth doing for correctness but did not lower this number, since it moves branches rather than removing them.
baseline._note_repository_wktlast: 128 -> 130 (2026-08-24): buildFeature/scanFeature gained an explicit wktLast flag. The old code skipped the last selected column unconditionally, assuming it was an AsText(geometry) result — so an attribute-only query silently lost its last real attribute (caught by the Cyprus/Greece golden fixtures, name_native came back empty). The two cases are indistinguishable from the row alone, so the flag cannot be inferred; +2 for a correctness invariant that a comment could not enforce.
baseline._note_spatialindex_batch: 67 -> 73 (2026-08-24): ResolveChains replaced the single-id ResolveChain (which is gone, not kept alongside) with a batched recursive CTE plus dedupeFIDs. It removes an N+1 of 234 round-trips per bearing request, and passing the seed set as one json_each parameter instead of 300-400 placeholders keeps the statement small and stable (p95 141 -> 91 ms). PointInPolygon also stopped selecting AsText, which was 70 of its 80 ms.
baseline._note_service_scope_and_spans: 77 -> 81 (2026-08-24): beginSection (one span per response section, opened before validation so a rejected request is still traced), SetTracer, and adminContaining (the request-scoped point-in-polygon cache — Locate and Bearing asked the same question twice per request, the response's largest single cost).
baseline._note_perfgate: New (2026-08-24), above the 50 default cap (67 as first measured, 70 after main was split into runSummarize/runGate to get every function under the function-complexity cap): the performance gate. It drives the committed request set, reads spans back through the span_summary MCP tool and compares them against perf/baseline.json — call counts as hard limits, durations as loose ceilings. The bulk is flag/IO/report plumbing rather than nested logic; every decision function is under the function_complexity cap and unit-tested.
baseline._note_tracecheck: New (2026-08-24), above the 50 default cap: the trace-coverage gate. It is an AST walker, so its complexity is inherent — one branch per node shape it has to recognise (receiver forms, context params, doc-comment exemptions, interface assertions). It exists because instrumentation has no failing test to protect it: the gazetteer shipped six service methods with no spans and nothing went red. Covered at 77%.
baseline._note_bearing_lazy_admission: 73 -> 81 (2026-08-24): lazy tier admission. The boundary-tier guard needs a database round-trip per candidate's admin lineage, and the code resolved all 300-400 of them before ranking — to answer a question the top-ranked candidate settles on its own (measured: 16 of 20 calls need exactly one lineage). Ranking is pure arithmetic, so ranking first and resolving lazily is free and provably lossless; verified on 60 committed coordinates, 60/60 bearing labels unchanged. ResolveChains p95 142.5 -> 3.5 ms, request p95 118 -> 36-50 ms, sequential throughput 12.5 -> 23.8 req/s. The +8 buys Order() on the salience strategies, firstAdmitted() and its growing-batch fetch (resolveInto). First attempt landed at 90; unifying the "in {X}" path onto the same firstAdmitted() and deleting the now-callerless newTierGuard took 9 back off, which is the part that was genuinely redundant rather than new.

function_complexity._default_cap_note: The single most complex FUNCTION in a file (McCabe). This is the real overall-complexity control: a function keeps its complexity wherever it lives, so moving it between files can't game this gate — the only way to pass is to actually simplify the function (or extract cohesive sub-functions). New functions must stay <= 10; the baseline freezes today's offenders at their current max so they can't grow, and should ratchet DOWN as they are simplified. Repo max today is 15.

baseline._note_app_gazetteer: 12 -> 13 (2026-08-23): one more guard clause in buildGazetteer for the startup contract check. The check itself was extracted into verifyPackageContract to keep this at +1; the remaining increment is the call site, which cannot be folded into an existing branch.
baseline._note_raster_repository: 15 -> 14 (2026-08-23): extracting the shared layerOf lookup out of QueryPoint. Ratcheted DOWN — the file-level sum went up for CoverageAt, but the most complex single function got simpler, which is the metric that cannot be gamed by moving code between files.

hotspot._note: A file is a hotspot when it is complex AND under-tested; new hotspots fail the build. Grandfathered files below are the current ones — remove them from 'allow' as their coverage improves.
hotspot._note_perfgate: tools/perfgate/main.go is grandfathered at 48% coverage. Its decision logic IS tested (budget checking hard vs soft, missing spans, per-group matching, baseline round-trip incl. known-issue preservation, request driving, report rendering). What is not covered is the MCP transport and the process wiring (main/os.Exit), which would need a hand-built MCP server to fake. Remove this entry if that gets written.
